questions.q: In the lab scenario, what is the first real step the architect takes before changing anything about the 12 HR integrations?
options: Migrating every integration straight to event-driven
Building an integration inventory documenting each integration's purpose, direction, authentication, and owner
Deleting all 12 integrations and rebuilding them from scratch
Switching every integration to Basic Auth for consistency
questions.explain: Lesson 12's inventory step comes first — you can't consolidate or fix what you haven't fully documented yet.

questions.q: What duplicate work does building the inventory reveal in the scenario?
options: Two integrations (#3 and #9) both independently pull organizational-chart data
All 12 integrations turn out to be identical
No duplication exists once the inventory is built
The payroll eligibility check is duplicated three times
questions.explain: Integrations #3 and #9, built two years apart by teams unaware of each other, are the duplicate-integration problem from Lesson 12 made visible.

questions.q: Which integrations get migrated to OAuth with the HIGHEST priority, and why?
options: The ones already on OAuth, because they're easiest to document
The three on the old, never-rotated API key, because an unrotated long-lived credential is a standing security exposure
The low-volume termination integration, because it changes least often
None of them need to change authentication at all
questions.explain: The never-rotated API key integrations represent the highest standing security risk, so Lesson 12's standard treats them as the top migration priority.

questions.q: Why does the new-hire record sync, specifically, get recommended for a move to event-driven integration?
options: Because event-driven is always the better default pattern
Because its volume has grown substantially and the business confirmed ServiceNow doesn't need an immediate response back
Because OAuth requires an event-driven pattern to function
Because request-response integrations are being banned enterprise-wide
questions.explain: Rising volume combined with no genuine need to wait for a response is exactly the case Lesson 13 identifies as the real argument for event-driven integration.

questions.q: What real, honest cost does the lab's plan call out for moving the new-hire sync to event-driven?
options: There is no cost; event-driven has no tradeoffs
The team must decide how to handle a possibly-duplicated event (e.g., running onboarding-task creation twice) and build monitoring for missed or delayed events
Event-driven integration cannot use OAuth
The HR system must be replaced entirely
questions.explain: This mirrors Lesson 13's point that event-driven resilience comes with real design questions around duplicate delivery and missed-event detection.
